capabilities.target: directory profile and group memberships via idp.read_user
user MFA methods and temporary pass issuance via idp.reset_mfa

inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt states that every reset needs analyst approval, but the design provides no equivalent approval gate for sending the temporary pass to the requester.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in queue tool for MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model and the analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket text. It does not decay with model capability, but it can fail under autonomy_increase or control_removal and may weaken operationally under high approval volume.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass recipient to verified account owner record instead of ticket requester
Human approval gate for sending temporary pass

findings.title: Credential recovery secret can be sent to an untrusted requester (TC1 lethal trifecta with account recovery egress)

attack_path.note: Requester identity is taken from the email sender, including contractors and vendors.
Agent looks up the user named in the ticket.
Agent resets MFA and causes a temporary pass to be issued after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is posted to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to look up the user, reset MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, the requester field is the email sender, and the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket rather than the account owner.
The analyst review covers idp.reset_mfa only; the artifact does not show approval of the later send action.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary-pass delivery to the verified account owner or another directory-backed recovery channel instead of the ticket requester.
Add a separate approval gate on cap.send_temp_pass that shows the exact recipient and pass-delivery channel from the system of record.

forecast.watch_signal: Any removal or narrowing of analyst approval on cap.mfa_reset, or workflow changes that let the agent execute resets without queue review.

findings.title: Raw-action analyst approval is exposed to approval fatigue and can authorize account takeover resets for untrusted requesters (TC9 variant under high volume)

attack_path.note: Untrusted email sender becomes the requester shown to the analyst.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine.
Approved reset removes MFA methods and issues a temporary pass.

evidence.observation: For MFA problems, the agent is directed to reset MFA and every reset needs analyst approval.
The analyst sees the raw action target, requester, and full ticket body before approving.
The queue shows exact target and full ticket text, but only two analysts cover about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, creating fatigue pressure.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, so untrusted requesters can reach the reset workflow.

recommendations.action: Reduce approval fatigue by rate-shaping the queue, adding stronger identity verification before reset requests enter the approval workflow, or requiring higher-friction review for externally sourced requests.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval volume per reviewer rises further, queue latency grows, or the reset workflow is changed so fewer requests receive per-action analyst review.

rating.rationale: The design gives an untrusted ticket source a path to confidential directory data, MFA reset, and irreversible delivery of a temporary pass to the ticket requester. The only declared structural approval gate covers cap.mfa_reset, not cap.send_temp_pass, so the highest-severity present path remains unmitigated. Manual validation only; scripts were not available in this environment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design, prompt, queue view, and runtime notes provided in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, IAM policy, or runtime enforcement configuration was provided, so credential scope and exact orchestration of cap.send_temp_pass were inferred from the artifacts.
No audit or delivery-channel details were provided for chat.send_temp_pass, so recipient verification and post-action detectability could not be credited.
